title: Resistance Curvature: Recognition, Polyhedral Structure, and Graph Products
summary: Resistance curvature, introduced by Devriendt and Lambiotte, is a novel discrete curvature notion defined through effective resistance. A graph is called resistance nonnegative if there exists a choice of positive edge weights for which the resistance curvature is nonnegative at every vertex. This property has a notable combinatorial interpretation in terms of random spanning trees: a graph is resistance nonnegative if and only if it admits a distribution on its spanning trees under which every vertex has expected degree at most two.
